title: Do Electric Cars Really EAT Their Tires? 🛞⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: Electric cars eat their tires. Myth or fact? Mostly fact.
A J.D. Power survey of over thirty-one thousand owners found E V drivers say their tires wear faster than they expected.
Reason one: weight. A typical battery pack weighs around a thousand pounds, and unlike a fuel tank, it never gets lighter as you drive.
Reason two: instant torque. Full twist from a standstill means quick launches scrub rubber off the tread.
So tire makers added a new rating, H L, for high load. Same size and pressure, about a quarter more load than a standard tire.
Smooth launches and regular rotations help. Would you trade a little range for longer-lasting tires? Follow EV Drive.
